key_insight: An operation-aware multimodal model achieved the best reported ICU readmission prediction by integrating patient data, processed clinical notes, and hospital workload signals.
clinical_relevance: Accounting for hospital workload alongside patient condition could inform ICU discharge risk assessment, but clinical benefit remains unproven.
method: Combined vital signs, ICD/DRG codes, admission flow, and departmental workload indicators.
Used multi-agent extraction and self-evolving retrieval-augmented generation to reduce template noise in clinical notes.
Fine-tuned a multimodal Transformer with layer-wise freezing and differential learning rates, alongside class reweighting and decision-threshold calibration.
evidence_signal: Across 20 independent runs on 20,000 MIMIC-III ICU stays with about 10.5% readmissions, the best model achieved AUROC 0.8288 ± 0.0110, PR-AUC 0.4373 ± 0.0310, and F1 0.4757 ± 0.0196.
watch_item: External and prospective validation are needed to establish whether performance generalizes across hospitals and improves discharge decisions without excessive alerts.
paper_title: Operation-aware Multimodal Clinical Decision Support System for ICU Discharge Risk Assessment
